root_cause.text: In the dm-cache passthrough invalidation path, invalidate_remove() performed an incomplete state transition for write-hit overwrite_bio handling by remapping the bio after cache invalidation but neither submitting it nor preserving it for later completion, leaving the write bio dropped and hung.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit message explicitly state that invalidate_remove() “sets up the remapping for the overwrite_bio but then drops it immediately without submission, causing write operations to hang,” and the patch removes the old remap-plus-`mg->overwrite_bio = NULL` logic from invalidate_remove() and replaces it with a new invalidate_committed() continuation that calls `dm_submit_bio_remap(bio, NULL)` and ends the bio via `overwrite_endio`/`invalidate_complete()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always complete overwrite bios and only assign a generic I/O error on pre-submission migration failure so existing bio status is preserved.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a conditional call that only invoked bio_io_error(mg->overwrite_bio) when !success and overwrite_bio was present with a new overwrite_bio block that always completes the bio via bio_endio(mg->overwrite_bio); before completion, it sets mg->overwrite_bio->bi_status = BLK_STS_IOERR only when the migration failed and the bio has no existing status.
intent_record.how: This change ensures overwrite_bio is always ended when present, preventing it from being left incomplete on both success and failure paths. On failure before the bio was issued, it now assigns a generic I/O error status, while preserving any error status already set by lower layers if the bio had already been submitted and completed with its own result.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a committed-stage invalidation worker that remaps and submits the overwrite bio to origin so cache invalidation can complete asynchronously.
intent_record.what: A new static workqueue callback function named invalidate_committed is added. It retrieves the migration object from the work_struct, extracts the cache, overwrite bio, and per-bio data, conditionally calls invalidate_complete(mg, false) when mg->k.input is set, initializes mg->k with invalidate_completed as the continuation, remaps the bio to the origin while clearing discard state using remap_to_origin_clear_discard(cache, bio, mg->invalidate_oblock), installs overwrite_endio as the bio completion hook via dm_hook_bio, and submits the remapped bio with dm_submit_bio_remap(bio, NULL).
intent_record.how: At runtime this introduces a new deferred invalidation path that, after any needed completion of prior input handling, prepares and submits the overwrite bio to the origin device with a specific endio handler and follow-up continuation. This enables the invalidation workflow to continue asynchronously through committed work processing rather than stopping after earlier stages.

intent_record.intent_summary: Run invalidate follow-up work after commit completion by switching to the committed continuation and removing premature bio remap/cleanup from invalidate_remove().
intent_record.what: The callback passed to init_continuation() in invalidate_remove() was changed from invalidate_completed to invalidate_committed, and the immediate calls to remap_to_origin_clear_discard(cache, mg->overwrite_bio, mg->invalidate_oblock) and setting mg->overwrite_bio = NULL were removed from this function.
intent_record.how: This defers the discard-remap and overwrite_bio cleanup work until the commit continuation runs instead of performing it immediately after continue_after_commit() is set up, ensuring the post-invalidation handling occurs only once the commit has actually completed.

bic_trace_step.reason:
The snippet contains the full passthrough invalidation path and specifically shows the vulnerable logic in `invalidate_remove()`. After successful invalidation, it does:

- `init_continuation(&mg->k, invalidate_completed);`
- `continue_after_commit(&cache->committer, &mg->k);`
- `remap_to_origin_clear_discard(cache, mg->overwrite_bio, mg->invalidate_oblock);`
- `mg->overwrite_bio = NULL;`
- `schedule_commit(&cache->committer);`

This is the incomplete state transition described by the root cause. The write-hit `overwrite_bio` is remapped to origin, but it is neither submitted (no `generic_make_request`, `accounted_request`, or `issue_after_commit` for that bio) nor preserved for later completion/submission. Immediately afterward, `mg->overwrite_bio = NULL;` drops the only reference.

Then `invalidate_completed()` calls `invalidate_complete(mg, !mg->k.input);`, and `invalidate_complete()` only errors the bio if `!success && mg->overwrite_bio` via `bio_io_error(mg->overwrite_bio);`. Because `mg->overwrite_bio` was cleared to NULL before commit completion, even failure will not complete/error the bio. On success there is also no completion/submission path for the bio at all.

Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not present in this version.
